items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: He said, "Well, I don't like this. This is my band, and I don't know what the tax is."

ctx.x: You told him to give you your money, huh, Danny?

So he paid me. He said, "Well, I don't like this. This is my band, and I don't know what the tax is." I said, "You heard what the man said." The rest of them is lookin' at me. And I said, "I quit." I look around, I couldn't find no pictures -- because you've got to write a written notice. I went in the toilet, got some toilet

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’m with Lucky Millinder. The band is jumping. Tab Smith. Arnold Adams. Wilbur De Paris.

ctx.x: Zildjian, they come in with cymbals. Never known to give a cymbal to nobody. You paid for a cymbal. All drummers is waiting ’til they get to somewhere out of Boston, where they had this factory. You could go in there and see them making cymbals. Zildjian. I’m with Lucky Millinder. The band is jumping. Tab Smith. Arnold Adams. Wilbur De Paris. All them people’s passing through that band. It’s one of them . . .
